result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not kindness, not peace, not "be nicer"—those are downstream effects. If every person woke up with an insatiable, joyful drive to *understand* how things actually work (the universe, themselves, each other, systems, history, incentives, their own biases), most of our worst problems would become solvable embarrassments instead of identity rituals.

Imagine a world where:
- People got the same dopamine hit from changing their mind with new evidence that they currently get from owning someone online
- Status came from discovering something true rather than defending something comfortable
- Education, politics, and culture rewarded asking better questions instead of having the "correct" answers

The amount of self-inflicted suffering we could eliminate is staggering. Wars, scams, conspiracy theories, toxic relationships, institutional decay—most of them rely on people preferring to *feel* right over *being* right.

Everything else I might want (multi-planetary civilization, abundant energy, extended healthy lifespans, actual wisdom) becomes much more likely as a side effect.

So yeah. Turn the whole species into curious apes again, but this time with better tools and less self-deception. The rest would follow.
